pr_title: Update `homebrew_packages` to include new prefix and allows specifying alternate prefixes
pr_body:
Update the `homebrew_packages` to search in both of homebrew's default locations. As well as to allow the caller to specify the `prefix` to search.

There's a lot of `fs::path` and back to strings and back again here. But a lot of that seems to pre-exist. 

Fixes: #7108

issue_context.title: Homebrew package list empty on Apple Silicon
issue_context.body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to osquery! -->

# Bug report

<!--
Please follow this template.
Before submitting an issue search for duplicates.
-->

### What operating system and version are you using?

macOS Big Sur 11.3.1 (Apple Silicon)

<!--
You can run the command bellow. Paste result within a code block.

osqueryi --line "SELECT version, build, platform FROM os_version;"
-->

### What version of osquery are you using?

osquery 4.7.0

<!--
You can run the line bellow. Paste the result within a code block.

osqueryi --line "SELECT version from osquery_info;"
-->

### What steps did you take to reproduce the issue?

`SELECT * FROM homebrew_packages;`

### What did you expect to see?

A list of installed homebrew packages.

### What did you see instead?

An empty list.

I suspect this is because the install location of homebrew has changed for systems running Apple Silicon.

**Intel**
`/usr/local/bin/brew`

**Apple Silicon**
`/opt/homebrew/bin/brew`

--

**Source Link**:
https://github.com/osquery/osquery/blob/master/osquery/tables/system/darwin/homebrew_packages.cpp
comments:
This looks like a bug, as the original poster reports.

I also notice that `genHomebrewPackages` does not take any constraints, so there is no way to point this to a different install directory. I think, ideally, osquery should (a) accept a hidden column specifying where homebrew is installed (b) look in both the default `/opt/homebrew` and `/usr/local` locations.

review_comments: minor naming nit on `userRequested`, perhaps intent is more clearer with something like `prefixConstraintPresent`? Thoughts?
The intent is to log if a user requested path is absent. But I wasn't sure if I'd use it for anything else. Could be `logWarnings` or something
There might be a better name than `prefix` too 🤷
gotcha -- I like `prefix`, because it's consistent with what homebrew uses, but whatever works!
